name: Zottman Curl
research: Both arms together (right mirrors left). Start: arms hanging, elev 7 / plane 56 / elbow 13, palms forward (axis +x, index outward). End: top of the curl, elbow 124, palms turned down (axis -x, index toward the midline = pronated). Angles from the approved dumbbell_curl clip; range per S1 Marcolin 2018 (123 +- 12 deg). The small +y (0.12) in both axes keeps the in-between frames from passing through a zero-length handle axis (a straight +x -> -x blend would hit (0,0,0) at the halfway frame). Fix 12 Nov (review: top dumbbells nearly touched, hands hidden behind the plates, palms-down did not read): top elbows a little out (elev 14 / plane 20, forearm folding forward and slightly out, bend [0.15,1,0]) -> hands at x +-0.29, gap between the inner plates ~0.21 m (was ~0.08); elbow 112 so the forearm points forward ~20 deg above level and the back of the hand faces up. Camera yaw -20 / pitch 32 looks down onto the knuckles between the plates, so the overhand grip reads. Why the turn matters: S2 Kleiber 2015, brachioradialis share higher when pronated. Facts: research/zottman_curl.json. 13 Nov 2026 (pics-fixes): QA said one arm looked half-curled with its dumbbell in the stomach: both arms are the same (side view), the front camera looked straight down the forearms. Camera now yaw -48 / pitch 18 so both forearms show their length. 13 Nov 2026 fresh review (look A, 384 px), NOT yet applied because renders were paused for the new look: minor - the end stops with the forearm about level (elbow 112); raise to about 130 so it reads as the top of the curl; palms-down must be readable.
